In the folded square pyramid, the two boundary edges \(EA\) and \(EC\) of the net meet, so vertices \(A\) and \(C\) coincide. Thus edge \(AB\) has endpoints \(A\) and \(B\).

- \(CD\) has endpoint \(C=A\), so it shares an endpoint with \(AB\).
- \(CE\) has endpoint \(C=A\), so it shares an endpoint with \(AB\).
- \(DE\) has endpoints \(D\) and \(E\); neither is \(A\) or \(B\).

Therefore the edge with no endpoint in common with \(AB\) is \(DE\).

\[
\boxed{\text{A: Edge }DE}
\]
